storyboard.title: The Silk Road: Ancient Networks of Trade and Ideas

scenes.heading: The Silk Road: Ancient Networks
scenes.subheading: A vast web linked East and West
scenes.narration: A vast web of routes linked East and West for over two thousand years.
It began at ancient Chang'an, now Xi'an, during the Han dynasty in the second century BCE.
Land routes stretched more than six thousand kilometers across Eurasia. Sea routes flourished from the second century BCE to the fifteenth century CE.

lines: Glass, gold, horses, gems also moved.
scenes.narration: Silk was the star commodity because it was valuable, light, and durable. Glass, gold, horses, gemstones, art, and spices also traveled far.
Papermaking moved from China to Central Asia and then to Europe. Paper helped spread Buddhism, Manichaeism, and Zoroastrianism.
Christianity reached west of China by the seventh century CE. Merchants mixed ideas with local cultures along the way.
The name Silk Road was coined by a German geographer in the late nineteenth century. It originally described Chinese silk moving west during the Han Empire.
Historians prefer Silk Routes to show the many land and sea paths. Networks reached beyond Central Asia to Africa and the Indian Ocean.
Trade declined after the Tang dynasty fell in the early tenth century. Maritime centers like Canton stayed busy.

scenes.text: It seeks to revive the legacy of the ancient Silk Road by fostering infrastructure, trade, and cultural connectivity across Asia, Europe, and Africa.
scenes.narration: Today the Belt and Road Initiative revives this legacy across Asia, Europe, and Africa.

Sea routes flourished from the second century BCE to the fifteenth century CE.

facts.text: The Silk Road was a network of Asian trade routes active from the second century BCE until the mid-15th century.
facts.quote: The Silk Road was a network of Asian trade routes active from the second century BCE until the mid-15th century.

facts.text: The land routes spanned over 6,400 km (4,000 mi).
facts.quote: Spanning over 6,400 km (4,000 mi) on land

facts.text: The name "Silk Road" was coined in the late 19th century.
facts.quote: The name "Silk Road" was coined in the late 19th century

facts.text: Historians sometimes prefer the term Silk Routes to describe the intricate web of land and sea routes.
facts.quote: some 20th- and 21st-century historians instead prefer the term Silk Routes, on the grounds that it more accurately describes the intricate web of land and sea routes

facts.text: The Maritime Silk Road began by the 2nd century BCE and flourished until the 15th century CE.
facts.quote: It began by the 2nd century BCE and flourished until the 15th century CE.

facts.text: The Maritime Silk Road was primarily established and operated by Austronesian sailors in Southeast Asia.
facts.quote: The Maritime Silk Road was primarily established and operated by Austronesian sailors in Southeast Asia

facts.text: Silk was the most popular commodity that traveled the Silk Road because it was expensive, easy to carry, and durable.
facts.quote: the most popular commodity that traveled the Silk Road was… silk

facts.text: Luxury goods such as gold, silver, horses, gemstones, art, and spices like nutmeg, cloves, and pepper traveled long distances on the Silk Road.
facts.quote: goods of great value, such as precious metals like gold and silver, horses, gemstones, art, and spices like nutmeg, cloves, and pepper

facts.text: The Romans traded glass products eastward along the Silk Road.
facts.quote: The Romans were particularly good at making glass products, which they traded to the east

facts.text: Papermaking technology spread from China to Central Asia and later to Europe via the Silk Road.
facts.quote: Paper moved from China to Central Asia and later to Europe along the Silk Road

facts.text: Christianity reached the area just west of China by the seventh century CE through Silk Road routes.
facts.quote: Christianity, which began in the Mediterranean world, reached the area just west of China by the seventh century CE

facts.text: Merchants and travelers spread innovations by mixing their knowledge and beliefs with local cultures and technologies along the Silk Road.
facts.quote: Their ideas often mixed with the cultures and technologies of the areas in which they arrived, which spread innovations to new places

facts.text: The Silk Road existed for 2500 years from the Han dynasty to the middle of the 19th century.
facts.quote: lasted for 2500 years from the Han dynasty to the middle of the 19th century

facts.text: The Silk Road originated from ancient Chang'an, now Xi'an.
facts.quote: originated from ancient Chang 'an (now Xi 'an)

facts.text: In 670 A.D., Tubo invaded the Hexi region.
facts.quote: In 670 A.D, Tubo invaded the Hexi region

facts.text: The 670 A.D. invasion caused no merchants on the road and towns lost their bustle.
facts.quote: There were no merchants on the road, and the towns along the route lost their usual bustle

facts.text: After the fall of the Tang Dynasty in the early 10th century, Silk Road trade saw a deathblow and declined quickly.
facts.quote: In the early 10th century, following the fall of the Tang Dynasty, the trade on the Silk Road saw a deathblow. The trade on the silk road declined quickly.

facts.text: China's feudal society was in long stagnation with slow change, preventing large-scale commodity circulation.
facts.quote: China's feudal society was in a long period of relative stagnation, and the change was very slow. The law of the economic development of China's feudal society caused the commodity to be unable to circulate on a large scale.

facts.text: The Silk Road Economic Belt (SREB) seeks to revive the legacy of the ancient Silk Road by fostering infrastructure, trade, and cultural connectivity across Asia, Europe, and Africa.
facts.quote: It seeks to revive the legacy of the ancient Silk Road by fostering infrastructure, trade, and cultural connectivity across Asia, Europe, and Africa.

facts.text: The modern Silk Road (MSR) aims to integrate these regions through an extensive network of transport corridors, seaports, economic zones, and development policies.
facts.quote: the modern Silk Road (MSR) aims to integrate these regions through an extensive network of transport corridors, seaports, economic zones, and development policies.

facts.text: The regions most deeply involved in the modern Silk Road network are South Asia, West Asia, and Africa.
facts.quote: Among the regions most deeply involved in this network are South Asia, West Asia, and Africa

facts.text: The Silk Road Economic Belt (SREB) is a strategic component of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI).
facts.quote: The SREB, as a strategic component of the Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)

facts.text: The modern Silk Road initiative has implications for sustainable development, economic diplomacy, environmental governance, and regional cooperation.
facts.quote: implications for sustainable development, economic diplomacy, environmental governance, and regional cooperation.

facts.text: The name "Silk Road" was first used by a 19th-century German geographer.
facts.quote: The “Silk Road” was a name first used by a 19th-century German geographer

facts.text: The term originally described the movement of Chinese silks westward during the Han Empire (206 BCE to 220 CE).
facts.quote: to describe the movement of Chinese silks westward during the period of the Han Empire (206 BCE to 220 CE)

facts.text: Today the term refers to extensive land and sea trade networks of Eurasia and Africa in ancient and medieval periods.
facts.quote: Today, it refers to the extensive land and sea trade networks of Eurasia and Africa in the ancient and medieval periods

facts.text: No single road existed; silk was an important commodity but far from the only thing exchanged.
facts.quote: no singular road existed and silk—while an important commodity—was far from the only “thing” exchanged along these networks

facts.text: Using the plural "Silk Roads" emphasizes the variety of economic, social, and cultural interactions and exchanges.
facts.quote: Broadening the term to the plural “Silk Roads” emphasizes the variety of economic, social, and cultural interactions and exchanges

facts.text: Some Silk Road networks extended far beyond Central Asia to include trans-Saharan and Indian Ocean trade routes.
facts.quote: some of which extended far beyond central Asia to encompass the trans-Saharan and Indian Ocean trade routes

facts.text: Paper helped spread Buddhism to China along the Silk Road.
facts.quote: Buddhism spread to China around the same time that paper became prevalent in the region

facts.text: Paper also helped spread Manichaeism and Zoroastrianism along the Silk Road.
facts.quote: Same with Manichaeism and Zoroastrianism.

facts.text: The Silk Road served as a channel for the spread of ideas and cultural interactions.
facts.quote: One of the central significances of the Silk Road is that it served as a channel for the spread of different ideas and cultural interactions

facts.text: Spices like cinnamon from Sri Lanka and cassia from China were coveted trade items.
facts.quote: Spices from East and South Asia, like cinnamon from Sri Lanka and cassia from China, were exotic and coveted trade items

facts.text: Spices mainly traveled by maritime routes rather than overland Silk Road routes.
facts.quote: they didn't typically travel the overland routes of the Silk Road. Instead, spices were mainly transported along an ancient maritime Silk Road

facts.text: Roman glassware has been found in burial mounds in China, Korea, Thailand, and the Philippines.
facts.quote: archeologists excavating burial mounds in China, Korea, Thailand and the Philippines have found Roman glassware among the prized possessions of the Asian elite

facts.text: Zhang Qian was dispatched from Chang'an on a diplomatic mission to Central Asia by the Han emperor in the second century B.C.E.
facts.quote: dispatched from Chang'an on a diplomatic mission to Central Asia by the Han emperor in the second century B.C.E.

facts.text: During the Han dynasty, Central Asians, Persians, and the Roman elite learned about Chinese silk through Zhang Qian's travels.
facts.quote: Central Asians, Persians, and the elite of the Roman Empire learned about Chinese silk through the travels of Zhang Qian

facts.text: Silk was traded for Fergana horses used in the imperial cavalry.
facts.quote: Silk was traded for the famous Fergana horses used in the imperial cavalry.

facts.text: At the height of the Tang dynasty, one million people lived inside Chang'an's walls and one million more lived outside.
facts.quote: At the height of the Tang dynasty a million peopled lived inside Chang'an's wall and a million more lived outside the wall.

facts.text: Buddhism was introduced to western China in the 1st century B.C.E., and clerics and pilgrims exchanged artistic and literary styles along the Silk Road.
facts.quote: Buddhism had been introduced to western China in the 1st century B.C.E., and clerics and pilgrims were often those who exchanged artistic and literary styles as they traveled along the Silk Road.

facts.text: The fall of the Tang in the early 10th century brought a decline in overland Silk Road trade, but Canton remained a major maritime trading center.
facts.quote: The fall of the Tang in the early 10th century brought a decline of trade along the overland Silk Road, but Canton continued to be a major maritime trading center

facts.text: Objects from the Fukinoki tomb in Nara, Japan show cultural and artistic influences that arrived via the Silk Road.
facts.quote: Objects, including those found in the Fukinoki tomb in Nara, demonstrate the cultural and artistic influences that arrived in Japan via the Silk Road.

facts.text: Early Chinese and Middle-Eastern objects from archaeological sites in Thailand reflect cultural exchange.
facts.quote: Early Chinese and Middle-Eastern objects from archeological sites in Thailand reflecting cultural exchange.

facts.text: Thailand acted as a land bridge between the mainland to the north and the archipelagos to the south as a meeting point for travellers by land and sea routes.
facts.quote: As a meeting point for travellers by land and sea routes, Thailand's situation in Southeast Asia acted as a land bridge between the mainland to the north and the archipelagos to the south.

facts.text: Archaeological finds in Thailand including coins, ceramics, and beads provide evidence of cultural interactions, migration, and settlement of various ethnic groups.
facts.quote: Archaeological finds, including coins, ceramics, and beads provide evidence of cultural interactions, migration, and the settlement of a variety of ethnic groups.

facts.text: Chinese rock inscriptions and thousands of petroglyphs have been discovered along the Silk Roads following the Hunza and Gilgit rivers in the Indus Valley, North Pakistan.
facts.quote: A great number of inscriptions have been discovered along the Silk Roads that followed the Hunza and Gilgit rivers, including thousands of petroglyphs on the banks of the Indus river.

facts.text: Imported foreign coins such as Byzantine, Sassanian, and Arabian coins, along with gold- and silver-ware, decorations, glassware, and Chinese silk serve as tangible evidence of significant trade along three routes within China.
facts.quote: relics such as imported foreign coins (e.g. Byzantine, Sassanian and Arabian), gold- and silver-ware, decorations, glassware and Chinese silk all serve as tangible evidence of significant trade along these three routes.

facts.text: The Silk Roads linked the civilizations of Eurasia for much of premodern history, starting as early as the second century B.C.E.
facts.quote: starting as early as the second century, B.C.E., if not earlier

facts.text: China, Central Asia, West Asia, and to a lesser extent Europe were connected by the Silk Roads.
facts.quote: China, Central Asia, West Asia, and, to a lesser extent, Europe, were placed in touch with each other via the Silk Roads

facts.text: The cultural impact of the Silk Roads can hardly be overstated.
facts.quote: their cultural impact can hardly be overstated

facts.text: Political influences of the Silk Roads were particularly significant during the era of the Mongol empire.
facts.quote: the political influences, particularly during the era of the Mongol empire, have only, of late, received much attention

facts.text: The Silk Roads can be used to teach political history, economic institutions, art, religions, technology, and geography.
facts.quote: Political history, economic institutions, art, religions, technology, and geography all can be discussed courtesy of the Silk Roads

facts.text: The Silk Roads provide a vehicle to interrelate many Asian civilizations.
facts.quote: many Asian civilizations can be interrelated through this glorious and colorful vehicle
